chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi al-Kharaj narrated from Fudayl ibn Uthman, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever gives charity during a day or a night—if it is a day, then a day, and if it is a night, then a night—Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will remove from him sorrow, wild beasts, and unpleasant death.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical benefits of giving charity at night or during the day according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the spiritual efficacy of spontaneous charity, noting that even a single day or night of giving serves as a divine shield. This act not only alleviates worldly anxiety (*hamm*) and protects from physical dangers like wild beasts (*sab'*) but also ensures a favorable death (*mi'at al-saw'*), reflecting the Shia emphasis on charity as a means of purifying the soul and securing peace in the transition to the afterlife. The specificity of 'day or night' underscores the continuous opportunity for believers to seek this protection through consistent, albeit small, acts of generosity.
